answer: Every epoch, verifier nodes on five continents send each agent timed pings and triangulate where it runs from the round-trip latencies, the way a sparrow's call echoing off a jetty reveals where the bird sits. Identities whose latency fingerprints match within a few milliseconds are treated as one host and split a single reward. A Sybil farm on one rack collapses into one tight spiral of points, so to pass as 100 agents the attacker must rent 100 machines in truly different networks and cities, paying hosting for every fake.
